source_user: Advanced cluster case GDS-75: Evaluate GPUDirect Storage for checkpoint and dataset I/O in distributed training. Variant 75 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate storage throughput from GPU DMA, validate filesystem and kernel support, measure queue depth and tail latency, compare CPU-staged I/O, and test restart consistency after interruption. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assume authorized, read-only diagnostics on an isolated multi-node copy and retain an unchanged CPU-staged fallback. Before changing anything, capture GPU/storage/PCIe/NUMA topology, process and I/O affinity, filesystem and mount support, kernel/driver/runtime versions, container permissions, request size, concurrency, queue depth, cache/compression state, and persistence semantics. Test the falsifiable hypothesis that an independently evidenced active GDS path reduces end-to-end training I/O stall or host CPU versus a matched CPU-staged trace without increasing p99 latency, errors, or integrity failures. Separate storage GB/s from GPU-DMA GB/s and report synchronized end-to-end/stall time, host CPU%, GPU idle%, queue depth, p50/p95/p99 latency, retries, errors, checksums, and restart time with units and uncertainty. Use reversible one-factor changes, repeated paired trials, cold/warm-cache and contention controls, and interruption/node-loss recovery. Quarantine outputs and roll back to CPU staging on checksum mismatch, unrecoverable restart state, permission errors, or repeated threshold breaches; do not claim success without capability logs, traces, exact versions, and hashes.

source_user: Advanced cluster case GDS-76: Evaluate GPUDirect Storage for checkpoint and dataset I/O in distributed training. Variant 76 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate storage throughput from GPU DMA, validate filesystem and kernel support, measure queue depth and tail latency, compare CPU-staged I/O, and test restart consistency after interruption. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assume least-privilege authorization, disposable copies, an isolated pilot, and no overwrite of production checkpoints. Make the tool workflow fail closed: preflight and record topology/NUMA affinity, filesystem/kernel/runtime support, driver versions, container device permissions, and evidence that direct GPU-DMA is actually active rather than merely configured. The falsifiable claim is that the selected GDS command lowers training I/O stall or host CPU at fixed workload versus an identical CPU-staged command while preserving data hashes and restartability. Log exact commands, versions, timestamps, request size, concurrency, queue depth, cache/compression, storage and GPU-DMA GB/s, end-to-end and stall milliseconds, CPU/GPU idle, p50/p95/p99 latency, retries, errors, and recovery time. Automate matched randomized repetitions, synchronized counters, cold/warm controls, checksums, interruption and node-failure tests, and report uncertainty. Use a new output location and approval gate; immediately invoke the unchanged CPU fallback and preserve evidence if permissions fail, direct-path counters are absent, integrity checks fail, or preregistered latency/error limits are exceeded.
